A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DriveLaW and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. Retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original nuScenes video-generation and NAVSIM planning results, component ablations, qualitative analyses and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds nuScenes planning, OpenDV generalization, nuPlan generation-horizon and H20 runtime evaluations.

M1.justification: The chained video/planning architecture, noise reinjection, first-denoising-step conditioning, flow-matching objective and three-stage training remain unchanged. Expanded RoPE and motion-prompt descriptions restate mechanisms already documented in v1, including Appendix A.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates video generation on nuScenes and planning on NAVSIM. v3 substantially broadens evaluated coverage with nuScenes open-loop planning and zero-shot video generation on OpenDV; nuPlan, already used for training, also receives explicit video-generation evaluation (Tables 3 and 8).

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained benchmark, representation and runtime comparisons is unchanged. Added evaluations reuse Epona without introducing a new comparison method. FSDrive is added as related work, while GEM is mentioned as protocol precedent; neither receives a new baseline result.

E3.justification: v3 adds distinct evaluation protocols: nuScenes open-loop L2 error and collision rates at 1/2/3 seconds and averaged, zero-shot OpenDV testing, nuPlan FVD at 24/40/80/100 frames, and H20 runtime measurements at 1024×512. Existing training settings and retained benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B.2 adds direct tests of out-of-domain generalization and sensitivity to prediction horizon, materially extending robustness analysis. B.4 extends efficiency analysis to H20 video and planning latency. Existing component ablations and qualitative cases remain; the latent-representation visualization is relocated rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added results retain this reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing scores remain unchanged, including FID 4.6, FVD 81.3 and NAVSIM PDMS 89.1. New Tables 3, 8 and 10 substantially expand results: DriveLaW versus Epona achieves average nuScenes L2 1.15 versus 1.25 m and collision rate 0.24% versus 0.36%, and OpenDV FID/FVD 4.6/72.9 versus 6.9/80.7. Exceptions include worse 1-second collisions (0.15% versus 0.01%), worse 100-frame FVD (296.1 versus 277.3), and slower H20 planning (0.71 versus 0.42 seconds), despite faster video generation (0.21 versus 1.06 seconds/frame).

T1.justification: Equations 1–9 retain the same latent updates, masking and noise-injection definitions, conditioning equations and flow-matching loss. No new formal assumptions, propositions, proofs or substantive derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same scientific claims about latent coupling, noise reinjection, progressive training and state-of-the-art nuScenes generation/NAVSIM planning. Additional experiments support these claims without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: New Appendix D acknowledges persistent high-motion artifacts despite noise reinjection, inference-latency limitations and deployment challenges. Appendix B.2 interprets the new generalization results and acknowledges Epona's advantage at 100 frames while arguing a quality–speed tradeoff. These materially qualify v1's benefit-focused discussion. The new planning-safety interpretation nevertheless overlooks the worse 1-second collision result.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-availability statement and repository address, clarifies that the BEVFormer visualization uses perspective-view backbone features before BEV query transformation, and specifies hardware/resolution for the new H20 measurements. Core implementation details remain unchanged. Actual repository availability cannot be verified from the PDFs alone.

R1.justification: v3 adds FutureSightDrive/FSDrive as reference 79 and briefly discusses its visual spatiotemporal Chain-of-Thought approach. It also adds explicit citations to the introduction's world-model categories. The central positioning of DriveLaW relative to parallel generation/planning methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes include light abstract/method editing, moving the latent-representation discussion from Section 4.3 to Appendix B.1, expanding appendix organization, and revising the author/contact block.

P2.justification: v3 removes v1's paradigm-comparison Figure 1, relocates the latent visualization from Figure 5 to appendix Figure 4 with a clarified caption, and adds Tables 3, 8 and 10. Other diagrams and qualitative panels are retained, with localized table reflow and renumbering.

improvement.justification: The added generalization, planning, horizon and runtime evaluations broaden empirical support while exposing practical tradeoffs, and Appendix D makes residual artifacts and latency limitations explicit. The feature-source clarification and code-access statement also improve documentation. These are useful gains for the unchanged method, but the new protocols remain sparsely described and the planning-safety summary overlooks worse 1-second collisions, limiting the overall improvement.
